system.name: Graphiti
system.one_liner: a Lean 4 framework for defining, formally proving, and applying correctness-preserving rewrites to dataflow circuits, used to add out-of-order execution to dynamic HLS designs

content.subject: how Graphiti parses a circuit into ExprHigh, matches and rewrites a subgraph via ExprLow, then iterates or outputs

elements.name: Dynamic HLS tool
elements.role: external front-end that compiles programs into dataflow circuits and receives the optimized circuit back

elements.name: Dot graph
elements.role: the dataflow circuit exchanged with the HLS tool in the dot graph input language

elements.name: ExprHigh
elements.role: Graphiti's higher-level graph representation, parsed from the dot graph and re-emitted after each rewrite

elements.name: matcher
elements.role: function that searches ExprHigh for a subgraph matching the selected rewrite's pattern

elements.name: Subgraph
elements.role: the matched subgraph that the rewrite will replace

elements.name: rewrite
elements.role: function that applies the rewrite to the matched subgraph on the lower-level representation

elements.name: ExprLow
elements.role: Graphiti's inductively defined low-level graph representation, more suited to verification, produced by the rewrite

relations.what: the front-end's dataflow circuit is exchanged as a dot graph
Graphiti parses the dot graph into ExprHigh
the matcher searches the current ExprHigh graph
the matcher returns the matched subgraph
the matched subgraph is passed to the rewrite function
ExprHigh has a corresponding ExprLow representation used to carry out and verify the rewrite
the rewrite is applied on ExprLow, which is more suited to verification
the rewritten graph is lifted back up from ExprLow to ExprHigh
Graphiti outputs the rewritten circuit back to the HLS tool, or loops back to rewrite it further

content.key_idea: Graphiti wraps a dataflow circuit in a verified rewrite loop: it parses the circuit into ExprHigh, matches a subgraph, rewrites it on the verification-friendly ExprLow representation, and lifts the result back up, iterating or emitting the optimized circuit.
content.reading_order: Left to right from the external HLS tool and dot graph into the green Graphiti box, then down through ExprHigh, matcher, Subgraph and rewrite to ExprLow, looping back to ExprHigh.

evidence: it accepts dataflow circuits, rewrites them using a verified rewriting framework, and can either continue iterating
A rewrite is selected and its matcher function is run to find a subgraph to be replaced
the resulting graph is lifted back up to ExprHigh, where it can be output or rewritten further

summary: Figure 1 gives a high-level overview of Graphiti's tool flow for verified dataflow-circuit rewriting. An external Dynamic HLS tool exchanges its circuit with Graphiti as a dot graph, which Graphiti parses into ExprHigh, its higher-level graph representation. A matcher function searches ExprHigh for a subgraph matching a selected rewrite's pattern; the rewrite is then carried out on ExprLow, an inductively defined lower-level representation better suited to formal verification. The resulting graph is lifted back up to ExprHigh, closing a loop that can either feed into another rewrite iteration or be emitted back to the HLS tool as the optimized circuit. A dashed boundary and colour separate Graphiti's formally verified internals (green) from the unverified front-end tool (red-brown), visually grounding the paper's claim that only the internal rewriting steps carry a correctness guarantee.

notes: Prior label 'walkthrough' corrected to 'anatomy': the figure has no numbered/lettered markers or step labels on arrows anywhere (checked the full source SVG text), which the v3 spec requires for walkthrough; this is a single chained pipeline (component internals + datapath) shown once, with ExprHigh/ExprLow each drawn twice to depict the loop back for iteration.
